**Novelty (originality, unexpectedness): 4**
Why? The solution introduces several highly original concepts that push beyond standard flexible-work policies. The "Firewall Rule" (legally insulating right-to-disconnect workers from presenteeism cultures) and the "Generational Bridge" (allowing younger staff to *earn* a 4-day week by automating legacy processes, thereby proving efficiency to skeptical older management) are particularly clever. While the overall structure of dividing offices into archetypes is a known HR strategy, the specific mechanisms used to bridge them are fresh and unexpected.

**Usefulness/Feasibility (practicality, implementability): 4**
Why? The policy is highly actionable, addressing the core operational friction points of global remote work. The "Follow-the-Sun Handoff Protocol" (3-minute EOD videos) and "Golden Overlap" windows directly solve cross-border collaboration issues. It loses a point only because the "Global Hourly Parity" model—pro-rating salaries to 80% and supplementing with a "Flex Retention Premium"—would be an administrative and legal nightmare to execute consistently across 12 different countries with varying tax structures, labor laws, and currency exchange rates. 

**Flexibility (multiple approaches, adaptability): 5**
Why? The solution excels here by explicitly avoiding a one-size-fits-all approach. It categorizes the 12 offices into four distinct archetypes and provides tailored solutions for each. Furthermore, it offers dual-track performance metrics (Impact Velocity vs. Relationship Velocity), splits roles into internal vs. client-facing, and provides multiple coverage models (Client Coverage Rotas, Coverage Pods, part-time agency staff) to ensure operations continue smoothly regardless of local schedules.

**Elaboration (detail, development): 5**
Why? The solution is exceptionally well-fleshed-out. It moves from high-level principles down to specific technological interventions (e.g., scheduled send defaults, calendar context integrations), structural changes (Local Flex Councils, Executive Sponsors), and precise operational workflows. It even addresses the psychological needs of the workers (e.g., abandoning staggered Fridays so employees get a continuous 3-day weekend) and the change management required to retrain managers from "supervisors" to "orchestrators."

**Cultural Sensitivity (cross-cultural appropriateness): 5**
Why? This is the strongest dimension of the solution. It deeply understands the underlying psychology of different global markets. Instead of dismissing "visible effort" cultures (like Japan or the UAE) as backward, it respects those external client expectations by keeping client-facing roles traditional while shielding internal teams. It also introduces "Rituals of Dedication" (Innovation Sprints, Client Crisis Swarms) to give employees in these cultures culturally acceptable avenues to demonstrate loyalty and "going the extra mile" without necessarily burning out in the office.
